description: Curated demo dataset for local development: requirements, tests, work items, and risks for a small todo web app with SQLite persistence.

nodes.title: Manage todo lifecycle
nodes.statement: The system shall allow an authenticated user to create, view, edit, and permanently delete todo items through the web UI. Each operation shall provide clear success or validation feedback.
nodes.notes: Source: Product brief §2.1 — Core user journeys

nodes.title: Track completion state
nodes.statement: The system shall allow a user to mark an open todo as done and to revert a completed todo back to open without losing title, description, or tags.

nodes.title: Filter todos by status
nodes.statement: The system shall provide list filters for all todos, open todos only, and completed todos only. The active filter shall be visible and shall persist for the duration of the session.

nodes.title: Persist todo data across restarts
nodes.statement: The system shall persist all todo fields in a local SQLite database so that data remains available after application or server restart. No in-memory-only storage shall be used for production demo mode.

nodes.title: Store optional description and tags
nodes.statement: The system shall support optional free-text description and a list of string tags on each todo. Empty description and an empty tag list shall be valid states.

nodes.title: Create todo from form
nodes.notes:
Covers happy-path creation including optional description and tags.

Precondition: Application is running; database is empty or isolated test fixture is loaded.

Test Steps: 1. Open the todo app in a browser.
2. Enter a unique title and optional description/tags.
3. Submit the form.
4. Verify the new item appears at the top of the list with the entered values.

Test Environment: Chrome latest, local Flask dev server

Test Expected Outcome: Todo is persisted and visible in the list without page reload errors.

nodes.title: Edit existing todo
nodes.notes:
Validates inline or modal edit flow updates persisted fields.

Precondition: At least one todo exists in the database.

Test Steps: 1. Create a todo with known title and description.
2. Open edit, change title and description, save.
3. Reload the page.
4. Confirm updated values are shown.

Test Expected Outcome: Stored record matches edited values after reload.

nodes.title: Delete todo with confirmation
nodes.notes:
Ensures destructive action requires explicit user confirmation.

Test Steps: 1. Create a todo.
2. Trigger delete and confirm the dialog.
3. Verify the item is removed from the list and absent after reload.

Test Expected Outcome: Todo row no longer exists in SQLite.

nodes.title: Toggle done state on checkbox
nodes.notes:
UI regression guard for completion styling and filter buckets.

Test Steps: 1. Create an open todo.
2. Click the completion checkbox; verify completed styling.
3. Click again; verify item returns to open styling.
4. Switch to Done filter and confirm visibility rules.

Test Expected Outcome: Status transitions are consistent in UI and database.

nodes.title: Filter open and done lists
nodes.notes:
Manual UX check; automate when filter endpoints are stable.

Test Steps: 1. Create two todos; mark one done.
2. Select Open — only open item shown.
3. Select Done — only completed item shown.
4. Select All — both visible.

Test Expected Outcome: Each filter shows the correct subset without stale rows.

nodes.title: Data survives server restart
nodes.notes:
Integration test for SQLite file persistence.

Precondition: SQLite database file path is configured for the demo environment.

Test Steps: 1. Create a uniquely titled todo.
2. Stop and restart the Flask process.
3. Reload the application.
4. Search the list for the unique title.

Test Expected Outcome: Todo still exists with identical field values.

nodes.title: Persist description and tags
nodes.notes:
Test Steps: 1. Create a todo with multi-line description and three tags.
2. Reload the page.
3. Open edit and verify description and tags are intact.

Test Expected Outcome: Optional fields round-trip through the API unchanged.

nodes.title: Edit flow cannot clear description
nodes.notes: When the browser edit prompt is cancelled, the UI keeps the previous description and shows no feedback — confuses reviewers during demos.

nodes.title: Add pagination for long todo lists
nodes.notes: Filtering works but rendering 200+ rows blocks the main thread on low-end laptops.

nodes.title: Validation messaging for empty titles
nodes.notes: API returns explicit 'Title is required.' and regression tests were added in the demo repo.

nodes.title: SQLite write lock under concurrent access
nodes.notes:
Demo uses embedded SQLite; parallel writes from CI and manual testing can surface 'database is locked'.

Category: technical

Occurrence: 4

Severity: 8

Mitigation Strategy: Move demo/staging to PostgreSQL; add bounded retry with exponential backoff on write paths; document single-writer constraint for local SQLite.

nodes.title: No authentication on todo API
nodes.notes:
Any client with network access to the dev server can mutate todos — acceptable for isolated local demo only.

Category: compliance

Occurrence: 6

Severity: 6

Mitigation Strategy: Gate demo deployments behind platform auth; require bearer tokens on mutating routes before shared environments.

nodes.title: Prompt-based editing reduces usability
nodes.notes:
Browser prompt() dialogs block accessibility tooling and feel inconsistent with the rest of the canvas UX.

Category: ethical

Occurrence: 7

Severity: 3

Mitigation Strategy: Replace prompts with inline form controls in the sidebar; add client-side validation mirroring API rules.
